units.text: INT. PYGMALION - CONTINUOUS

Tell her so, Governor: tell her so. I’m willing. It’s me that suffers by it. I’ve no hold on her. I got to be agreeable to her. I got to give her presents. I got to buy her clothes something sinful. I’m a slave to that woman, Governor, just because I’m not her lawful husband. And she knows it too. Catch her marrying me! Take my advice, Governor: marry Eliza while she’s young and don’t know no better. If you don’t you’ll be sorry for it after. If you do, she’ll be sorry for it after; but better you than her, because you’re a man, and she’s only a woman and don’t know how to be happy anyhow.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: Pickering: if we listen to this man another minute, we shall have no convictions left.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: To Doolittle.
Five pounds I think you said.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Thank you kindly, Governor.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: You’re sure you won’t take ten?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Not now. Another time, Governor.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: HIGGINS [handing him a five-pound note] Here you are.
Thank you, Governor. Good morning.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: [He hurries to the door, anxious to get away with his booty.
When he opens it he is confronted with a dainty and exquisitely clean young Japanese lady in a simple blue cotton kimono printed cunningly with small white jasmine blossoms.
Mrs. Pearce is with her.
He gets out of her way deferentially and apologizes].
Beg pardon, miss.
Garn! Don’t you know your own daughter?
units.name: THE JAPANESE LADY

units.text: DOOLITTLE {exclaiming Bly me! it’s Eliza!
HIGGINS {simul- What’s that!
This!
PICKERING {taneously By Jove!
Don’t I look silly?
units.name: LIZA

units.text: Silly?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: PEARCE
units.name: MRS

units.text: at the door.
Now, Mr. Higgins, please don’t say anything to make the girl conceited about herself.
units.name: MRS

units.text: HIGGINS [conscientiously] Oh!
Quite right, Mrs. Pearce. [To Eliza] Yes: damned silly.
Please, sir.
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: HIGGINS [correcting himself] I mean extremely silly.
I should look all right with my hat on.
units.name: LIZA

units.text: She takes up her hat; puts it on; and walks across the room to the fireplace with a fashionable air.
A new fashion, by George! And it ought to look horrible!
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: DOOLITTLE [with fatherly pride] Well, I never thought she’d clean up as good looking as that, Governor.
She’s a credit to me, ain’t she?

I tell you, it’s easy to clean up here. Hot and cold water on tap, just as much as you like, there is. Woolly towels, there is; and a towel horse so hot, it burns your fingers. Soft brushes to scrub yourself, and a wooden bowl of soap smelling like primroses. Now I know why ladies is so clean. Washing’s a treat for them. Wish they saw what it is for the like of me!
units.name: LIZA

units.text: I’m glad the bath-room met with your approval.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: It didn’t: not all of it; and I don’t care who hears me say it. Mrs. Pearce knows.
units.name: LIZA

units.text: What was wrong, Mrs. Pearce?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: PEARCE
units.name: MRS

units.text: blandly.
Oh, nothing, sir. It doesn’t matter.
units.name: MRS

units.text: I had a good mind to break it. I didn’t know which way to look. But I hung a towel over it, I did.
units.name: LIZA

units.text: Over what?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Over the looking-glass, sir.
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: Doolittle: you have brought your daughter up too strictly.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Me! I never brought her up at all, except to give her a lick of a strap now and again. Don’t put it on me, Governor. She ain’t accustomed to it, you see: that’s all. But she’ll soon pick up your free-and-easy ways.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: I’m a good girl, I am; and I won’t pick up no free and easy ways.
units.name: LIZA

units.text: Eliza: if you say again that you’re a good girl, your father shall take you home.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Not him. You don’t know my father. All he come here for was to touch you for some money to get drunk on.
units.name: LIZA

units.text: Well, what else would I want money for? To put into the plate in church, I suppose.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: She puts out her tongue at him.
He is so incensed by this that Pickering presently finds it necessary to step between them.
Don’t you give me none of your lip; and don’t let me hear you giving this gentleman any of it neither, or you’ll hear from me about it. See?
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: Have you any further advice to give her before you go, Doolittle? Your blessing, for instance.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: No, Governor: I ain’t such a mug as to put up my children to all I know myself. Hard enough to hold them in without that. If you want Eliza’s mind improved, Governor, you do it yourself with a strap. So long, gentlemen.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: He turns to go.
